coaching.summary: The decision structure captures the core tension between protecting concentrated enterprise revenue and enabling bottom-up adoption, but several causal pathways and constraints need sharpening before analysis can be trusted.

strengthen_items.label: Make customer migration cost an explicit constraint
strengthen_items.detail: The brief notes that several large accounts 'would pay less under usage pricing,' implying a floor on acceptable revenue loss that should be modeled as a hard constraint on the NRR outcome rather than left implicit.

strengthen_items.label: Surface the expansion-revenue upside risk for usage pricing
strengthen_items.detail: The current structure only shows enterprise churn as a risk; adding a corresponding upside risk — that usage-based exposure could drive expansion revenue beyond seat caps — would balance the causal picture around the NRR outcome.

strengthen_items.label: Reframe the goal to make the two success criteria separable
strengthen_items.detail: NRR above 110% and bottom-up adoption are currently bundled into one goal node, which can mask trade-offs; separating them into distinct sub-goals would let you see when an option advances one at the expense of the other.

strengthen_items.label: Add a sales-team execution capacity constraint
strengthen_items.detail: Pricing complexity and execution risk is already present, but the brief implies a simultaneous migration across a large installed base, so an explicit constraint on internal capacity to manage concurrent pricing conversations would make that risk more actionable.

elements_considered_but_excluded: A 'competitor pricing moves' outcome node was considered but competitive pressure is already represented as a factor.
A 'customer contract length' constraint node was considered but the brief references renewal timing only in passing, not as a structural driver.

bias_signals.detail: The brief frames the risk almost entirely as downside — 'several of them would pay less under usage pricing' — without articulating scenarios where usage pricing grows those same accounts beyond their current seat caps.

The brief states a specific NRR target of 'above 110%' as though it is achievable across all options, without acknowledging that the top-account concentration ('40% of revenue') makes that threshold highly sensitive to the behavior of just a handful of accounts.
